title: LinkedIn announcement
intro: The one-sentence claim, the three keys, the privacy proof, the link. Written in the first person for Hugo's own profile; the paragraph in brackets is optional and easy to drop. LinkedIn shows the first three lines before "…more", so the claim has to be in them.
copy:
I built a dictation app for the Mac that never touches the internet. It's called Timbre, it's free, and today it's public.

Hold a key and talk. Let go, and cleaned-up text lands wherever your cursor is: filler gone, punctuation right, your phrasing intact. Not a transcript of what you said — what you meant to type.

Three keys, no window, no tour:
→ Hold right Option: dictate into any app.
→ Tap left Option: hear a selection read back.
→ Hold right Command on a selection and say fix, shorten, explain or plain. Say a to-do with nothing selected and it lands in Apple's Reminders.

The part I care about most: out of the box, Timbre makes zero network requests. Not "we don't sell your data". None. Speech recognition and the cleanup both run on Apple's on-device models. Point Little Snitch at it and watch nothing happen. Turn on update checks and it makes exactly one request, to my own site, carrying nothing about you. Every request it can ever make is listed on the site.

No account. No subscription. Notarized by Apple. Source on GitHub.

[I'm a Flutter and React Native developer who had never written Swift. Timbre is the project I learned it on, and every decision along the way — what to build, what to refuse — is written down as a decision record you can read.]

It needs macOS 26 on Apple Silicon with Apple Intelligence on.

Download: https://timbre.hugopretorius.dev

#macOS #Swift #Privacy #Dictation #IndieDev

Notes

  • Lead with the claim; the link goes last, because LinkedIn buries posts whose first line is a link.
  • One image: the light-mode hero screenshot (pill mid-dictation over the keyboard). A 30-second clip does better than a still if it's ready; see the demo script.
  • Reply to the first comment with the "how it was built" link: Backstage › Decisions.
  • Post on a weekday morning. Do not edit the post in the first hour; edits reset distribution.

title: Product Hunt listing
intro: Everything the Product Hunt form asks for, in the order it asks. Tagline is limited to 60 characters; the description to 260.
status: draft — prepared, not necessarily launched the same day
copy:
**Name:** Timbre

**Tagline:** Mac dictation that never touches the internet

**Description:** Hold a key, talk, release: cleaned-up text lands wherever your cursor is, cleaned by Apple's on-device model. Read any selection aloud, fix or shorten it by voice, say a to-do into Reminders. Zero network requests, no account, free.

**Topics:** Mac, Productivity, Privacy, Artificial Intelligence, Developer Tools

**First comment (maker):**

Hi Product Hunt — I'm Hugo, and I made Timbre because every dictation app I tried wanted my voice on its servers.

Timbre runs on Apple's on-device speech and language models, so out of the box it makes no network requests at all. That's a falsifiable claim, not a policy: run Little Snitch or `nettop -p Timbre` and the list stays empty. The only request it can ever make is an update check you turn on yourself, and the site lists it.

What it does:
• Hold right Option and talk: filler gone, punctuation right, your phrasing intact, pasted into any app.
• Tap left Option: hear a selection read back, with the best voice on your Mac.
• Hold right Command on a selection: say fix, shorten, plain or explain. A silent hold means fix. Command-Z undoes.
• Hold right Command with nothing selected: say a to-do and it lands in Apple's Reminders, dated.

It learns your words — vocabulary, corrections, definitions — in a dictionary that lives on your Mac.

Free for personal use. macOS 26, Apple Silicon, Apple Intelligence on. Source on GitHub, and every product decision is a written record you can read. Happy to answer anything.

title: The 30-second demo
intro: One take, screen only, no voice-over — the captions carry it. Record at 1920×1200 with the menu bar hidden, light mode, a plain desktop. Every shot is an action the viewer could repeat in the next minute.
html:
Shot list

At Shot Caption
0:00 Mail compose window, cursor in the body. Hold right ⌥; the pill appears: "Waking the mic…" then live words with filler. Hold a key. Talk.
0:06 Release. "Cleaning up…", then the clean sentence pastes in. Let go. Cleaned-up text lands where your cursor is.
0:11 Select "timber kit" in the sentence, hold right ⌘, say "fix". It becomes "TimbreKit". Hold on a selection. Say fix.
0:16 Select "ADR", hold right ⌘, say "explain". The card slides in: "Architecture Decision Record — from your dictionary". Or explain. Your definitions answer first.
0:21 Nothing selected. Hold right ⌘, say "call the dentist Thursday". Reminders opens on the Timbre list with the item dated. Say a to-do. It's in Reminders, on your phone too.
0:26 Select the paragraph, tap left ⌥. The reading pill appears; the cursor moves through the text. Tap to hear it back.
0:29 Cut to the wordmark over the keyboard illustration, rainbow stripe. Zero network requests. Free. timbre.hugopretorius.dev

Before recording

  • Settings › Dictionary: "timber kit → TimbreKit" taught; "ADR" defined.
  • Reminders open in a second Space so the switch is one swipe.
  • Enhanced voice installed (Settings › Reading says which).
  • Rehearse the right ⌘ holds: the mode arms after 350 ms, and "fix" fires on the word.
  • nettop -p Timbre running in a Terminal window off-screen — useful for a still, not for the clip.

After

  • Export at 1080p and as a GIF under 8 MB for the README.
  • The still for LinkedIn is the 0:06 frame; for Product Hunt, 0:16.

title: Screenshots
